items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: And incidentally speaking, Manuel Perez, he is my godfather.

ctx.x: He began with the old method, which often you've heard before, with the solfege. It was singing and for ear training. And then after when he thought I was ready to start on the instrument, then he sent me to Lorenzo Tio Jr.

But how long did he work with you on the solfege? The workman was just about nine months. I know Manuel Perez, they say, did that. And the Tio's too would make you sing a long time. And incidentally speaking, Manuel Perez, he is my godfather. Oh, is that right? Yeah, my godfather. Yes, right. He was my godfather. And by the way, the clarinet then was your first instrument? It is. Yeah, the clarinet was my first instrument. Did you ever want to take up drums? Or were you ever curious about them when your father…
And when I first began on the clarinet, because of my fingers being short, I had to use a C clarinet.
